learner_level: medical students and early clinical trainees
description: Expanded undergraduate ophthalmology blueprint with core anatomy, examination, disease systems, emergencies, investigations and OSCE reasoning. Each topic produces six mixed-format draft cards; faculty must map local learning outcomes and supply authoritative references before approval.

topics.name: Ocular anatomy and physiology
learning_objectives: Describe the fibrous, vascular and neural coats of the eye
Trace aqueous humour production, flow and drainage
Relate ocular structures to common clinical signs

topics.name: Ocular history and examination
learning_objectives: Take a focused ophthalmic history including onset, pain, laterality and risk factors
Perform and interpret visual acuity, pupils, fields, motility and red-reflex checks
Recognize findings requiring urgent ophthalmology review

topics.name: Optics, refraction and low vision
learning_objectives: Explain emmetropia, ametropia and accommodation
Differentiate myopia, hyperopia, astigmatism and presbyopia
Describe refraction principles and low-vision support

topics.name: Eyelids, lashes and orbit
learning_objectives: Recognize common eyelid malpositions and lid lesions
Differentiate preseptal from orbital cellulitis
Identify proptosis patterns and orbital red flags

topics.name: Lacrimal system
learning_objectives: Describe tear production and drainage anatomy
Differentiate epiphora causes and lacrimal obstruction
Recognize acute dacryocystitis and its complications

topics.name: Conjunctiva and ocular surface
learning_objectives: Differentiate allergic, viral and bacterial conjunctivitis
Recognize subconjunctival haemorrhage and other benign red-eye causes
Identify red-eye warning signs that suggest corneal or intraocular disease

topics.name: Cornea and sclera
learning_objectives: Recognize corneal abrasion, ulcer and keratitis presentations
Describe corneal examination and fluorescein staining
Differentiate episcleritis from scleritis and identify sight-threatening disease

topics.name: Lens and cataract
learning_objectives: Classify common cataract types and risk factors
Assess visual disability and indications for referral
Outline cataract surgery principles, complications and postoperative warning signs

topics.name: Glaucoma
learning_objectives: Differentiate primary open-angle and angle-closure glaucoma
Interpret intraocular pressure, optic disc and visual-field findings
Recognize and outline urgent management principles for acute angle closure

topics.name: Uveitis and ocular inflammation
learning_objectives: Classify uveitis by anatomical location
Differentiate anterior uveitis from conjunctivitis and keratitis
Recognize systemic associations and urgent complications

topics.name: Retina and macula
learning_objectives: Recognize age-related macular degeneration patterns
Differentiate common macular and retinal disorders
Interpret central visual loss and metamorphopsia symptoms

topics.name: Diabetic and vascular retinopathy
learning_objectives: Classify diabetic retinopathy and maculopathy
Recognize hypertensive and retinal vascular occlusive disease
Explain screening principles and sight-threatening features

topics.name: Vitreous and retinal detachment
learning_objectives: Differentiate posterior vitreous detachment from retinal tear and detachment
Recognize flashes, floaters and curtain-like field loss as warning symptoms
Describe urgent assessment principles

topics.name: Neuro-ophthalmology
learning_objectives: Localize visual pathway lesions from field defects
Differentiate optic neuritis, ischemic optic neuropathy and papilloedema patterns
Assess anisocoria, relative afferent pupillary defect and cranial nerve palsies

topics.name: Ocular motility, diplopia and strabismus
learning_objectives: Differentiate monocular from binocular diplopia
Assess ocular movements and common cranial nerve palsies
Describe cover tests, concomitance and basic strabismus patterns

topics.name: Pediatric ophthalmology and amblyopia
learning_objectives: Recognize amblyopia risk factors and screening principles
Identify leukocoria and other urgent pediatric eye signs
Describe common childhood strabismus and refractive problems

topics.name: Ocular trauma and chemical injuries
learning_objectives: Recognize open-globe injury and avoid harmful examination steps
Outline immediate first aid for chemical eye injury
Differentiate blunt, penetrating and superficial ocular trauma

topics.name: Ocular infections
learning_objectives: Differentiate microbial keratitis, endophthalmitis and orbital infection
Recognize contact-lens-associated infection risk
Identify postoperative and post-traumatic infection red flags

topics.name: Systemic disease and the eye
learning_objectives: Recognize ocular manifestations of diabetes, hypertension and thyroid disease
Relate autoimmune and inflammatory disease to ocular findings
Identify medication-related ocular adverse effects that require review

topics.name: Ophthalmic investigations and imaging
learning_objectives: Choose appropriate initial tests for common ophthalmic presentations
Interpret principles of tonometry, visual fields, OCT and fundus imaging
Recognize limitations and safety considerations of investigations

topics.name: Ophthalmic pharmacology and procedures
learning_objectives: Describe major ophthalmic drug classes and safety principles
Recognize important topical medication adverse effects and contraindications
Explain indications and basic principles of common ophthalmic procedures

topics.name: Integrated ophthalmology OSCE and emergencies
learning_objectives: Structure an eye examination station and present findings clearly
Approach sudden visual loss, painful red eye and acute diplopia
Prioritize referral and initial management in common ophthalmic emergencies
